Grouped, Event-Stratified V-Fold Cross-Validation for Start/Stop Data

Source: R/subject_folds.R
subject_vfold_cv.Rd

`subject_vfold_cv()` builds [rsample::group_vfold_cv()] folds that keep all of a subject's intervals in one fold and, when `status` is given, stratify by the subject-level event status of [add_subject_status()]. `subject_nested_cv()` does the same for both the outer and inner folds of an [rsample::nested_cv()] object. The folds work with every start/stop function that takes resamples: [nested_cv_coxnet()], [cv_coxnet()], [tune_grid_start_stop()], [tune_race_start_stop()] and [fit_resamples_start_stop()].

Usage

subject_vfold_cv(
  data,
  subject_id,
  status = NULL,
  v = 5,
  repeats = 1,
  event = 1,
  pool = 0.1,
  keep_status = FALSE,
  ...
)

subject_nested_cv(
  data,
  subject_id,
  status = NULL,
  outer_v = 5,
  inner_v = 5,
  repeats = 1,
  event = 1,
  pool = 0.1,
  keep_status = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per interval.

subject_id

The subject identifier column, as a string.

status

The event column, as a string, or `NULL` (default) for grouped folds without stratification.

v

The number of folds. `subject_nested_cv()` takes `outer_v` and `inner_v`.

repeats

The number of repeats of the outer folds.

event

The value of `status` that marks an event (default `1`). A factor or character `status` is matched on its labels, so a factor with levels `"0"`/`"1"` works as is, and one with levels `c("censored", "event")` needs `event = "event"` (an `event` that is not a label is an error). A logical `status` counts `TRUE` as the event (`event` must be logical, or a value that coerces to logical without producing `NA`, e.g. `1`/`0`). A numeric `status` needs a numeric or logical `event`.

pool

Passed to [rsample::group_vfold_cv()]: strata holding fewer than this share of the subjects are pooled.

keep_status

Keep the helper column in the splits' data: `subject_status`, or `.subject_status` if a column of that name already exists in `data` (the existing column is left in place).

...

Passed to [rsample::group_vfold_cv()] (to both the outer and the inner folds in `subject_nested_cv()`). In practice only `balance` is forwarded usefully, as `rsample` accepts no other extras. `group` and `strata` cannot be passed through `...`: they are set by these functions (and `v` is not a `subject_nested_cv()` argument either). Pass `v`, `repeats` and `pool` — `outer_v`/`inner_v` for `subject_nested_cv()` — as direct arguments instead.

outer_v, inner_v

The number of outer and inner folds.

Value

An `rset` (`subject_vfold_cv()`) or a `nested_cv` object (`subject_nested_cv()`).

Details

The stratification column only exists while the folds are built: with `keep_status = FALSE` (default) it is removed from the data the splits hold, so a `y ~ .` formula or recipe does not pick it up as a predictor. If `data` already has a `subject_status` column, the helper is named `.subject_status` instead and the existing column is left in place.

See also

[add_subject_status()]

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("rsample", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  long <- data.frame(
    id = rep(1:40, each = 2), start = rep(c(0, 1), 40), stop = rep(c(1, 2), 40),
    status = rep(c(0, 1), 40) * rbinom(80, 1, 0.5), x = rnorm(80)
  )
  folds <- subject_vfold_cv(long, "id", status = "status", v = 4)
  nested <- subject_nested_cv(long, "id", status = "status", outer_v = 4, inner_v = 3)
}
# }
